title: Movement & Sequence
description: Learn sequence through Python inputs, calculations and output, then apply the same ordered reasoning to the knight's route and a purchase activity.
learning_objective: Trace values and movements in order; read whole-number inputs, calculate with variables and print results in Python; explain why each step must follow the previous one.

title: Making Decisions with If
description: Use Python if statements to reason about optional actions, then connect true-or-false checks to guarded game movements and a fuel-warning activity.
learning_objective: Write and trace a Python if statement, distinguish conditional from unconditional instructions, test a boundary value, and connect the same decision to can() checks in the game.

title: Choosing Between Two Actions
description: Express two alternative actions with Python if/else, test equality at a decision boundary, and apply the same branch reasoning to game routes and an affordability activity.
learning_objective: Trace exactly one branch of Python if/else, place calculations in the appropriate branch, handle equality deliberately, and justify both game-route alternatives.

title: When Actions Change the Situation
description: Track changing values in Python and changing mechanisms in the game; use the updated situation to make a decision in the balance activity.
learning_objective: Trace a variable before and after an update, make a decision using the current value, and order game actions so the required door or plate state is maintained.

title: Repeating Instructions
description: Use Python for loops to repeat a known number of steps and accumulate a result, then connect the pattern to game repeat commands and totaling item prices.
learning_objective: Trace a Python for/range loop for zero, one and several repetitions, initialize and update a running total, and distinguish repeated actions from one-time steps in the game.

title: Repeating While Something Is True
description: Use Python while loops to repeat until a changing condition becomes false, then connect stopping rules to game corridors and a savings-target activity.
learning_objective: Trace the check/body/update cycle of a Python while loop, justify its stopping condition, handle reaching or exceeding a target, and compare conditional loops with fixed-count game repetition.

title: Plan, Try, and Improve
description: Combine Python sequences, decisions, updates and loops; use traces and boundary tests to debug both a game plan and the ticket-counter activity.
learning_objective: Decompose a problem, trace a decision inside a Python loop, diagnose initialization/count/boundary mistakes, and justify corrections using test evidence and game-state checkpoints.
